findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Address the migration-apply clobber: specify how value_wo_version=1 avoids re-sending CHANGEME over the already-seeded live values on the FIRST apply (e.g. sequence/plan-review the migration so no value_wo is sent, or require immediate operator re-seed as part of the same maintenance window), and correct the Approach text that currently claims the seeded value 'is never clobbered' without distinguishing the migration transition from steady state.
evidence: Plan asserts value_wo 'is only (re)sent when value_wo_version changes' and concludes the seeded value 'is never clobbered' — but the migration itself changes value_wo_version from absent to 1, satisfying that very send condition.

dd30 ticket evidence: the three target params exist in live state holding real seeded values (jira-api-token 'version 2 ... is_CHANGEME=false'; cookie-signing-secret and opcert-ed25519-key are the same out-of-band-seeded pattern).

The plan does not distinguish the first (migration) apply from subsequent refreshes; the deferred operator ticket AC lists 'apply -> verify no SecureString value ... -> rotate crown-jewels' but frames rotation as post-exposure hygiene, not as recovery from a placeholder-clobber the migration apply itself would cause.
findings.finding: The plan's no-clobber contract holds only in steady state; the one-time migration apply (value_wo_version transitions unset -> 1) is itself a version change, so the AWS provider will SEND value_wo="CHANGEME" and overwrite the live operator-seeded secret value with the placeholder for all three already-seeded parameters.
findings.location: Approach section — 'value_wo = "CHANGEME" + value_wo_version = 1 preserves the create-placeholder + operator-seed + no-revert contract (write-only value is only (re)sent when value_wo_version changes ... so the operator's out-of-band value is never clobbered)'
scenarios: Operator runs the migration terraform apply against prod; value_wo_version goes unset->1; provider PutParameter sends 'CHANGEME'; the live jira-api-token / cookie-signing HMAC / opcert Ed25519 key are overwritten with the placeholder, breaking bridge tools, invalidating all SSO sessions, and disabling op-cert signing until re-seeded.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm (via `terraform plan` in the deferred operator ticket, and state it in the runbook) that migrating `value` -> `value_wo`/`value_wo_version` is an in-place update with no forced replacement, so the live operator-seeded secret is not transiently reset to `CHANGEME`.
evidence: Plan: 'the operator's out-of-band value is never clobbered and `user_data.sh`'s `CHANGEME` fail-fast still fires on an unseeded slot'
Plan: 'terraform validate ... (static; no plan/apply against the real backend)' — so update-vs-replace behavior is never observed
Absence: no statement that `terraform plan` shows an in-place update (no `-/+` replacement) for the three migrated resources
findings.finding: The plan asserts the operator's out-of-band seeded value is 'never clobbered' during the value->value_wo migration, but never confirms that changing `value` -> `value_wo` on `aws_ssm_parameter` is an IN-PLACE update rather than a destroy/recreate. If the provider treats the schema change as forcing replacement, the create step re-sends `value_wo = "CHANGEME"`, transiently resetting the live seeded secret to the placeholder (and firing user_data.sh's fail-fast) — a data-loss/availability event the plan's no-clobber claim would contradict.
findings.location: Approach / '`value_wo = "CHANGEME"` + `value_wo_version = 1` preserves the create-placeholder + operator-seed + no-revert contract ... never clobbered'
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the runbook/operator-remediation ticket an explicit pre-apply gate: run `terraform plan` and verify each migrated `aws_ssm_parameter` shows an in-place update (`~`), not replacement (`-/+`); document rollback if a replacement is detected.

findings.checklist_item: Reconcile the no-clobber claim with the value_wo_version=absent->1 transition on the migration apply: either prove Terraform does NOT re-send value_wo when the resource pre-exists in state (cite provider behavior), or make the ordering explicit (accept the CHANGEME re-send and mandate re-seed+rotate immediately after apply) and add a DATA LOSS RISK note.
evidence: Plan: 'write-only value is only (re)sent when value_wo_version changes, and is never compared/stored, so the operator's out-of-band value is never clobbered'
The migration is precisely a value_wo_version transition (absent -> 1), which by the quoted rule triggers a (re)send of the CHANGEME placeholder onto live secrets
user_data.sh CHANGEME fail-fast implies a CHANGEME write would break every container that reads the clobbered slot
DATA LOSS RISK: the deferred prod apply could overwrite 20 seeded crown-jewel secrets with 'CHANGEME'
findings.finding: The plan's central safety claim — that migrating `value`/`ignore_changes` to `value_wo`+`value_wo_version = 1` never clobbers the live operator-seeded secret — is internally inconsistent with its own stated rule that the write-only value is '(re)sent when value_wo_version changes.' On the migration apply, `value_wo_version` transitions from absent to 1 (a change), which would re-send `value_wo = "CHANGEME"` and overwrite ~20 live crown-jewel SecureStrings with the placeholder. The plan does not reconcile or assert against this clobber.
findings.location: Approach ("value_wo = \"CHANGEME\" + value_wo_version = 1 preserves ... no-revert contract") / AC line 8 (deferred operator apply)
scenarios: Operator runs the deferred `terraform apply`; each for_each member of rebar_secrets (plus opcert key + cookie secret) gets value_wo re-sent as CHANGEME, overwriting the live seeded value
Containers reading a clobbered SecureString hit the CHANGEME fail-fast and fail to boot
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach, add the provider-behavior citation for what happens to value_wo on the apply where value_wo_version first appears on an already-created parameter; if a re-send occurs, sequence the deferred operator ticket as apply -> re-seed all 20 slots -> rotate crown-jewels, and mark it DATA LOSS RISK.

evidence: Plan: 'write-only value is only (re)sent when value_wo_version changes, and is never compared/stored, so the operator's out-of-band value is never clobbered'

scenarios: After operator seeds the real key out-of-band, a subsequent terraform apply with unchanged value_wo_version=1 unexpectedly re-writes CHANGEME, reverting the crown-jewel secret

findings.checklist_item: Specify a back-out path and a post-migration/post-rollback state assertion for the deferred prod apply (e.g., verify each SecureString still resolves to its seeded value, or compensate-forward by re-seeding), and require the operator ticket to confirm no slot is left at CHANGEME.
evidence: Plan Testing: only 'terraform validate ... passes (static; no plan/apply against the real backend)' and defers the apply
No mention of a rollback path if the apply half-completes across the 18-member for_each + 2 singletons, nor of the state/secret condition after a revert
ABSENCE: no assertion that live secret values remain intact after a partial-failure or a rollback (revert versions.tf + resources)
findings.finding: No back-out path or post-rollback-state assertion is specified for the deferred prod migration apply. Because the change narrows a read path (Terraform stops reading the secret into state) and is a one-way transformation of how state records are interpreted, T11 requires asserting on state AFTER rollback, not merely that apply/validate succeeded. The plan asserts only `terraform validate` exit 0 and 'no SecureString value in terraform state pull' post-apply, with nothing covering a partial or reverted apply.
findings.location: Testing / Acceptance Criteria (AC line 5 terraform validate; AC line 8 deferred operator apply)
scenarios: Migration apply fails partway through the for_each; some params now on value_wo, some still on value; operator reverts the commit
Post-rollback, some slots were re-sent as CHANGEME and are not restored, leaving production secrets in a broken/placeholder state
